area.title: Journey flow, step order and what applies when
area.scope: How the notification journey hangs together across pages: the version mount and session, the step order and next-page rules, the opening run, change and return contexts (from hub, from review, from template review), the shared journey buttons and their actions, the status strip and reference, the obligations and scope rules saying which questions apply to which consignment and what is optional versus a hard stop, the prototype route and coverage tables, and the tests repo journey scope and conditional-rule specs. Stops at any one page content and at journeys walked whole (whole-journeys). Includes the high-risk plants frontend flow, entry guard, section captions, route registration, obligation manifest and cross-page fit specs.

sources.role: the answers to the two notification view header questions the 25 November re-distil raised from ruling:sam-2026-11-19 point 2. It settles c-438: once the amend confirmation page exists, 'Amend this notification' on the header is a link to that page rather than a posting button, because the first click then changes nothing, a POST that only renders a page is the wrong verb and leaves a re-POST on the back button without JavaScript, and Delete already opens its confirmation page by href in the same header; Copy as new keeps its own form because it still changes something, Delete stays a link, and no action shares another's form, in live animals, germinal products and plants alike. Point 2 of the 19 November ruling is unweakened, its subject being that no action shares another action's form, which a link does not do. It settles c-447 the other way from the default: the plants header gains a Copy as new action so both journeys offer the same three actions. That is wiring rather than a feature build, because every layer beneath it is already on main - the plants backend serves POST /{referenceNumber}/copy with a NotificationCopyMapper, the plants frontend's real and stub persistence both implement copy, and its engine holds copyJourney - and only the header's copyAction and route are missing. The plants backend therefore needs nothing and trade-imports-plants-backend does not join this programme's repos; inc-123 takes plantsfrontend alongside backend, frontend and tests, and inc-124's stale-copy return takes plants too. Plants' copy carries plants' own answers, so the carried-over-trade against cleared-shipment split is read against plants' own fields rather than copied field for field.

sources.role: the decision that pagination is kept everywhere and that its earlier removal was an error: every address book list and every address picker pages, and no requirement says a list of an organisation's addresses is served or shown unpaginated. It drops req-611's 'unpaginated' clause and supersedes ruling:ian-2026-11-23 point 6 on that point alone, because that point's reasoning rested on the address book's list endpoint taking no role and so having to be read whole and paged for display, which is no longer true of the service: RequestedListFilters takes roles and searchRoles, AddressController lists one page at a time with page and pageSize, and ListPaging sets 1 to 100 defaulting to 25, exactly the bounds ruling:paul-2026-11-05 point 8 names. The role filter runs in the service before the page is cut, so paging the API cannot make it wrong, and Paul's point 8 stands in full. The rest of ruling:ian-2026-11-23 stands: the pickers page at eight, the one-page clause of inc-087's criteria 7, 8 and 9 stays dropped with req-594 and req-595, and the 'Selected address' restatement comes back with the paging. EUDPA-827 is the fix and has landed on the animals frontend's main. It settles conflict c-292 by keeping the plants contact picker's pagination and inset, and the contact picker pages at eight rather than five, confirmed by Ian the same day, so every picker in both journeys pages at the figure the INS address book list already uses and ruling:ian-2026-11-23 point 1 set for the other pickers.

sources.role: the decision on transporter management, outranking ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm on that point and lifting claim c-285: the address book manages transporters as per-organisation records, and adding one mid journey uses the address book hand-off already built for addresses (inc-077, inc-078, inc-080). A transporter is its own record in its own transporters collection inside the address book service, not the Address model; it has no roles and stores a private-or-commercial type instead; a commercial transporter country is forced to XI (Northern Ireland) with no reference-data lookup, while a private transporter keeps its choice of export country. Approved transporters are parked.

claims.statement: This ruling settles whether the service manages transporters at all and, if so, whether the address book or something else does - the question ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm point 5 (claim c-285) left blocked pending requirements.
claims.quote: On transporter management, which Sam's ruling of 9 October (afternoon) left blocked pending requirements — whether the service manages transporters at all and, if so, whether the address book or something else does (`ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm` point 5, claim c-285):
claims.note: answers the block ruling:sam-2026-10-09-pm point 5 left, recorded there as claim c-285

claims.statement: The address book manages transporters, which are saved per organisation just like other addresses.
claims.quote: My decision is that the address book will manage the transporters, just like other addresses which are saved per organisation.

claims.statement: Adding a transporter uses the same pattern of moving to the address book mid journey that adding other addresses uses.
claims.quote: It will use the same pattern with moving to the address book mid journey, like other addresses when adding transporters - it's essentially the same pattern.

claims.statement: The earlier block rested on the concept of 'approved transporters': a list that may be managed in MDM for all organisations and added to each organisation's own transporter options.
claims.quote: I think that previous ruling was based on the concept of 'approved transporters' which may be a list managed in MDM for all organisations that will be added to the organisations individual transporter options.

claims.statement: Approved transporters are not to be worried about for now.

sources.role: the decision on what the address book stores for an address's type and uses (EUDPA-711): "use" is renamed "role" everywhere, in the record, the API, the code, the copy keys, the tests and the spec, and an address holds the roles it can play on a notification, being place of origin, consignor, consignee, importer, place of destination and branch address. The address book stores roles only and requires at least one; it does not store an address type and ignores one a client sends, the address type being the INS front door's grouping of roles worked out from them. The grouping of roles into sending, receiving and branch is the address book's internal rule rather than part of its API, and it refuses roles from more than one group, and a consignee, importer or place of destination outside the United Kingdom. The list takes role, repeatable and any-of, and searchRole, in place of addressType, use and searchUse. A role a new notification type needs is added in code, each role in exactly one group. Addresses saved before the change are not migrated: after release the addresses collection is dropped in dev and test with CDP tooling and the address book restarted, and locally the stack is restarted. The address book's list and every address picker keep pagination even though the Design Release 2.1 prototype has none, the list API paging with page and pageSize of 1 to 100 defaulting to 25, because organisations in test environments hold thousands of addresses; no requirement to list an organisation's addresses unpaginated is built, which ruling:ian-2026-11-23 point 6 later reads the other way for req-611 and so outranks on that point alone.

sources.role: the owner's decisions: outranks every other source. Search boxes use the real frontend's accessible component with MDM's entries. JavaScript behaviour follows the toolbox rule with graceful degradation; JavaScript-only prototype behaviour, pop-ups included, waits on design in its own theme. Commodity catalogue and search wait on MDM; transporter management waits on requirements; the INS dashboard's summary information waits on its requirements. The overview, review, declaration and confirmation are set-owned, and shared parts change add-only. Where plants has the same page or behaviour, the same increment changes it. Each notification list is reframed in its own frontend. The report groups work as ready or blocked. Claims marked as the orchestrator's apply Sam's principles and are not his rulings; ruling:sam-2026-10-09-templates covers templates and the dashboard narrowing.

claims.statement: Sam rules that, as a pre-step for these increments, three questions are answered: is it possible with off-the-shelf GDS; if not, with other complementary off-the-shelf components; if not, why is the atypical thing strongly required. The ruling limits DR1 use to clashes between 'the real frontend' and the prototype; it does not say which frontend that is, or whether DR1 judgements apply to differences in the INS frontend, the backends or other repos.
The ruling does not say which override wins when a DR1 judgement and a real constraint the prototype cannot express point different ways on the same difference.
The ruling does not say what a real service does where a real constraint overrides the prototype: whether it keeps today's behaviour or matches the prototype as closely as the constraint allows.
The ruling does not say whether a feature or behaviour a real service has that Design Release 2.1 does not show at all counts as a difference to remove, or is left alone.
The ruling does not say what to do where the code two themes need to touch overlaps, so no boundary keeps their pull requests from conflicting.

sources.role: the target design: what every page, field, option, hint, error message, branch and journey step should be. Wins by default.

claims.statement: Design release 2.1 is served under the base path /design-release-2.1.
claims.quote: const DESIGN_RELEASE_21_BASE = '/design-release-2.1'

claims.statement: Every route of the root router is copied under /design-release-2.1 (each method of each route, with the same handlers), so DR2.1 has the same pages and handlers as the root journey rather than its own route table.
claims.quote:
versionRouter.use(middleware)
    copyRouterStack(sourceRouter, versionRouter)

claims.statement: Only route layers are copied into the version router: router-level middleware and the catch-all _all method are not copied.
claims.note: mechanism: copies the root router's route table into the version router.

claims.statement: The versions are mounted in the order Testing 4, Testing 3, Testing and then Design release 2.1; the longer /testing paths go before /testing so they are not taken as /testing paths. No separate design release 2 version is mounted.
claims.quote:
// Mount the longer /testing* paths before /testing so Express does not treat them as that route
mountTesting4Version(govukPrototypeKit, router)
mountTesting3Version(govukPrototypeKit, router)
mountTestingVersion(govukPrototypeKit, router)
mountDesignRelease21Version(govukPrototypeKit, router)

claims.statement: Under /design-release-2.1 the session data a page sees is a separate nest stored under the session key _designRelease21, so DR2.1 notifications, drafts and answers are kept apart from the root journey and the other versions.
claims.quote: sessionKey: '_designRelease21',

claims.statement: Inside the DR2.1 session nest the flag _isDesignRelease21Version is set to true on every request, which handlers use to tell they are running as DR2.1.
claims.quote: nest[versionFlag] = true

claims.statement: Two session keys are shared across all versions rather than kept in the DR2.1 nest: the addresses added to the address book (addressBookAddedAddresses) and the submitted notifications (submittedNotifications). Reading or writing them in DR2.1 reads or writes the shared value.
claims.quote:
const SHARED_SESSION_KEYS = [
  'addressBookAddedAddresses',
  'submittedNotifications'
]

claims.statement: When a DR2.1 request carries a form or query field (not starting with an underscore, not the session key and not a shared key) whose name also exists in the shared session outside the DR2.1 nest, the nest takes the outer session's value for that key before the handler runs.
claims.note: mechanism: copies outer session values into the version nest. The posted value itself is applied later by the prototype kit. Recorded as observed, not interpreted further.

claims.statement: Before a DR2.1 response redirects or ends, the session is restored so the DR2.1 nest is saved back under _designRelease21 in the full session.
claims.quote:
root[sessionKey] = nest
    req.session.data = root
claims.note: mechanism: saves the version session nest.

claims.statement: Every DR2.1 page is given the requested URL, query string included, as currentPath.
claims.quote: res.locals.currentPath = req.originalUrl

claims.statement: In DR2.1, a redirect to a journey path is prefixed with /design-release-2.1 (for example a redirect to /notification-hub goes to /design-release-2.1/notification-hub), and a redirect to / goes to /design-release-2.1.

A link or redirect to / with a query string (/?...) becomes /design-release-2.1?... in DR2.1, and a journey path keeps its query string and fragment after the prefix; whether a path is a journey path is decided on the path without its query string or fragment.

In DR2.1, every string in the data passed to a page render that is a journey path is prefixed with /design-release-2.1, so links, form actions and back links built by handlers stay inside the version.

claims.statement: Every request into the set enters the set's context before authentication runs, and every route is wrapped so it runs in that context.
claims.note: mechanism: carries the ambient set id through a request so set-keyed stores (dispatch index, journey flow, obligations, records, session) resolve to this set.

claims.statement: The entry guard runs before every handler in the set and, when it names a target, redirects there and stops the request.
Boot refuses the set when two pages both claim to collect the same obligation, naming the obligation and both pages.
Boot refuses the set when any obligation that is not system-populated is collected by no page, naming each uncovered obligation.
An obligation id may not contain a path metacharacter ('.', '[' or ']'), and boot refuses one that does.
claims.quote:
const ID_UNSAFE = /[.[\]]/
...
      throw new Error(
        `Obligation id "${obligation.name}" (at ${templatePath}) contains a path ` +
          `metacharacter ('.', '[' or ']') — ids must be path-safe`
      )

claims.statement: Boot also refuses the set when a feature's fulfilment bindings do not cover every obligation, and when a party binding is not scalar.
claims.quote:
assertObligationPurity()
        assertFulfilmentBindingCoverage()
        assertPartyBindingsAreScalar()
claims.note: The assertion names say what they refuse; the assertion bodies live in bridge/fulfilment-registry.js and features/addresses/assert-party-bindings.js, outside this part's slice.

claims.statement: A derived page or section gate consulted before the obligation-to-page index is built raises an error rather than silently gating every page and section out.
claims.quote:
throw new Error(
    'Derived gate consulted before the dispatch index exists — call ' +
      'buildDispatch() at boot first (an empty index would silently gate ' +
      'every page and section out)'
  )

claims.statement: Reading the obligation-to-page index before boot answers as if it were empty rather than raising, so the gate layer can tell the un-booted case apart itself.
claims.note: mechanism: the set-keyed dispatch store, which holds the obligation owner, collects, slug and validation maps per page.

claims.statement: The journey flow is unconfigured until boot calls configureJourneyFlow, and asking it for a row status, the INS type-question URL or an entry-guard target before then raises 'journey flow not configured'.

The set configures its journey flow from eight things: the sections, the task rows, the row-status rule, the INS type-question URL, the flow-only keys, the entry-guard target, the layout and the section-caption lookup.
claims.quote:
configureJourneyFlow(SET_ID, {

claims.statement: A page claims an obligation by naming it in the `collects` list on the page's meta, and the page that claims a group also owns every obligation nested inside it, because ownership is resolved by walking up the obligation's dotted path to the nearest claimed ancestor.
A page that states validation rules can have them run against already-stored answers by a caller holding only its page id, which is how the task list and the review page re-check saved answers.
The start section holds one page, the dashboard.
The about-the-consignment section holds three pages in order: origin, commodities and import reason.
The description-of-the-goods section holds three pages in order: consignment details, animal identification and additional details.
The transport-and-arrival section holds three pages in order: port of entry, transit countries and transporters.
The documents section holds one page, accompanying documents.
The consignment-parties section holds three pages in order: CPH number, permanent address and addresses.
claims.note: CPH number and permanent address come before the addresses page in the flow, although the addresses task row leads with the addresses page.

claims.statement: The review section holds three pages in order, the notification view, the declaration and the confirmation, and opens only when the journey is ready for check your answers.
The review section is the only section with an authored gate; every other section's availability is derived from its obligations.
claims.quote: gate: (scope) => scope.readyForCheckYourAnswers,
claims.note: No other section entry in the sections array carries a `gate` key.

claims.statement: A journey is ready for check your answers when every task row leaves the trader nothing to do, that is when each row reads fulfilled, not applicable or optional.
claims.quote:
/** True for a status that leaves nothing for the trader to do: fulfilled, not
 * applicable or optional. */
export const rowReady = (status) =>
  status === FULFILLED || status === NA || status === OPTIONAL

export const readyForCheckYourAnswers = (answers, inScope, evaluation) =>
  journeyTaskRows().every((row) =>
    rowReady(journeyRowStatus(row, answers, inScope, evaluation))
  )

claims.statement: A page with no authored gate applies when at least one obligation it collects is in scope; a page that collects nothing always applies.
An authored gate on a page replaces both the derived scope test and the required-earlier-answer test, so a page that states its own gate is never held back for a missing earlier answer.
claims.quote:
const prerequisitesAllowPage = (page, scope) =>
  Boolean(page.gate) || earliestMissingAnswerPage(page.id, scope) === undefined

export const pageGatePasses = (page, scope) =>
  prerequisitesAllowPage(page, scope) && pageAppliesTo(page, scope)

claims.statement: A section's prerequisite answers are those of its first page, so a section is held back by the same earlier answers its first page needs.
A page is held back only by those enforced answers whose own page comes earlier than it in the journey's page order, so an enforced answer asked later in the flow never blocks an earlier page.
claims.quote:
const continueOwnersBefore = (flowIndex) =>
  continueObligationOwners().filter(
    (owner) => owner.flowIndex !== -1 && owner.flowIndex < flowIndex
  )

const continuePrereqsBefore = (flowIndex) =>
  continueOwnersBefore(flowIndex).map((owner) => owner.id)

claims.statement: When a trader reaches a page whose required earlier answers are missing, they are sent to the page that asks for the earliest missing one in page order, and the page they tried to open is recorded with every missing answer id.
Save and continue goes to the next page in journey order that applies to this consignment, skipping any page that does not apply.
claims.quote:
const next = pages
    .slice(index + 1)
    .filter(isStep)
    .find((page) => pageAppliesTo(page, scope))
  if (!next) {
    return undefined
  }

claims.statement: Only a page that is not a sub-page and belongs to a task row counts as a step Save and continue can land on.
The permanent address page is in the journey's sections but in no task row, so it is reachable only from another page, not from the task list.
claims.quote: pages: [cphNumberPage, permanentAddressPage, addressesPage]
claims.note: The 11 task rows list the CPH number page (inside the addresses row) but never the permanent address page.

claims.statement: Past the last step of the journey, Save and continue has no next page to offer.
Pressing Save and continue on a page that is in no journey section raises an error naming the page.
A task row's link opens the first of its pages whose gate passes, and falls back to the row's first page when none does.
The task rows shown under a section are those whose first page sits in that section, ordered by where that page falls in the section.
claims.quote:
const firstPageIndexIn = (section, row) =>
  section.pages.findIndex((page) => page.id === row.pages[0].id)

export const taskRowsOfSection = (section) =>
  journeyTaskRows()
    .filter((row) => firstPageIndexIn(section, row) !== -1)
    .sort(
      (rowA, rowB) =>
        firstPageIndexIn(section, rowA) - firstPageIndexIn(section, rowB)
    )

The import reason task row covers the import reason page alone.

The animal identification task row covers the animal identification page, counts only the animal identifiers of each commodity line, is shown as a conditional row, and reads not applicable until the consignment has at least one commodity line.

claims.statement: The addresses task row groups two pages, the addresses page and the CPH number page, and does not read as finished until every animal that needs a permanent address has one, even when all the answers the two pages collect are given.

A row's status is worked out in three steps: a row whose condition does not apply reads not applicable; otherwise the row's parts are rolled up into a status; and a rolled-up fulfilled is demoted to in progress when the row's extra answer is still missing.
A row that does not author its own parts counts the obligations its pages collect, so the task list follows the dispatch ownership map by default.
claims.quote:
export const rowParts = (row) =>
  row.parts ?? row.pages.flatMap((page) => collectsOf(page.id))

claims.statement: A section's status rolls up every obligation its pages collect, in page order.
claims.quote:
export const sectionObligationIds = (section) =>
  section.pages.flatMap((page) => collectsOf(page.id))

export const sectionStatus = (section, answers, inScope, evaluation) =>
  statusOf(sectionObligationIds(section), answers, inScope, evaluation)

claims.statement: A task row whose already-saved answers no longer pass its own pages' rules is demoted back to 'To do' on the overview, however complete the engine counts it.
A row's stored-answer errors are its pages' stored-answer errors merged, and a page that states no rules of its own contributes none.
claims.note: mechanism: merges each page's stored-answer error map for one task row.

claims.statement: A card on the review page shows one broken-answer message, the first its rows produce, not every one behind it.

The entry guard applies to any page path under /live-animals/notifications/<journeyId>/ and leaves the create path, the four notification action paths and the origin page (with anything under it) alone.
A trader who opens a guarded page of a notification with no answer entered yet is sent to that notification's origin page.
That redirect is logged once at info with the notification's id and the path the trader asked for, under the message 'No answer entered, sent to the first page'.
claims.quote:
request.logger.info(
    { journeyId: journey.journeyId, path: request.path },
    'No answer entered, sent to the first page'
  )

claims.statement: A notification counts as having committed answers when any stored key is a trader-entered obligation (not a system-populated one) and holds an answer; a flow-only key such as the declaration does not count.
claims.note: A flow-only key is not in the obligation manifest, so obligationByName returns undefined for it.

claims.statement: The link that leaves a notification goes to that notification's overview once any answer is committed, and back to the dashboard while none is.
claims.quote:
export const leaveJourneyLink = (journey, answers) =>

    ? hubPath(journey.journeyId)
    : dashboardPath()

claims.statement: The question that asks which type of notification this is lives on the INS frontend, at /notification-type with the notification id and the current notification type ('live-animals') as query parameters.

Nothing in the set's flow sends a trader to the INS notification-type question: the entry guard's only target is the notification's own origin page, and the INS URL is handed to the journey flow for some other caller to use.
claims.quote:
export const journeyInsTypeQuestionUrl = (...args) =>

claims.note: The part's scope expects the entry guard to say when a trader is sent back to the INS type question. entry-guard.js returns only the origin page path, and the INS URL is exposed through journeyInsTypeQuestionUrl for a caller outside this part's files. Looked in entry-guard.js, journey-flow.js and routes-live-animals.js; the caller that uses it is not in this slice.

claims.note: CANCEL_AMEND_SLUG is 'cancel-amend' and the delete page's slug is 'delete', so the four paths are .../amend, .../cancel-amend, .../copy and .../delete.

claims.statement: Flow-only answers are kept in their own cookie, separate from the notification's answers, so none of them is part of the notification that is submitted.

---

  Object.fromEntries(
    flowOnlyKeys()
      .filter(

      )

claims.statement: The country of origin is always asked and always mandatory.
The country-of-origin subdivision code is always in scope and always optional.
Whether a region-of-origin code is required is itself always asked and mandatory.

The region-of-origin code is always in scope, and it switches from optional to mandatory when the trader answers yes to whether a region code is required; the reason given is that a region code is required.
claims.note: This is the only gate in the set that keeps an obligation in scope on both branches, so the answer is never purged when the requirement flips to no.

claims.statement: The arrival date at the port is always asked and always mandatory.
The port of entry is always asked and always mandatory.
The transporter type is always asked and always mandatory.
The commercial transporter record is asked, and mandatory, only when the transporter type is Commercial, and a stored commercial transporter is dropped when the type is switched away from Commercial.
The private transporter record is asked, and mandatory, only when the transporter type is Private, and goes out of scope otherwise.
The commercial and private transporter records are mutually exclusive: only one of the two can be in scope for any transporter type.
claims.quote: // Transporter type + mutually-exclusive address blocks

claims.statement: The means of transport is always asked and always mandatory.
The transport identification is always asked and always mandatory.
The transport document reference is always asked and always mandatory.

The countries transited are asked of rail and road consignments only, and even then they are never compulsory: a trader who passes through nowhere they can name leaves the list empty, the row reads Optional and submission is not held up.
claims.note: An existing ruling: the comment records it as a design release 1 decision.

claims.statement: A conditional obligation whose in-scope decision names no mandate is treated as mandatory, so an optional conditional answer must say 'optional' outright.
claims.quote:
// `status` must say 'optional' outright — `effectiveStatus` falls back to
// 'mandatory' for an implication that carries none.

claims.statement: The place of origin is always asked and always mandatory, and is stored as one composite address record.
The consignor is always asked and always mandatory.
The consignee is always asked and always mandatory.
The importer is always asked and always mandatory.
The place of destination is always asked and always mandatory.
The reason for import is always asked and always mandatory.
The purpose in the internal market is asked, and mandatory, only when the reason for import is internalMarket, and any stored purpose is dropped when the reason changes.
The destination country is asked, and mandatory, only when the reason for import is transit or transhipmentOrOnwardTravel, and is otherwise out of scope and purged.
claims.note: An existing ruling: the code records the V4 data dictionary (Confluence page 6497338582) as the authority for this rule.

claims.statement: The port of exit is asked, and mandatory, only when the reason for import is transit or temporaryAdmissionHorses, and is chosen from the same port list as the port of entry.
The exit date is asked, and mandatory, only when the reason for import is temporaryAdmissionHorses, and is otherwise out of scope and purged.
The internal reference number is always in scope and always optional.
The notification's approved reference number is assigned by the system when the notification is created and is never entered by a trader; it is mandatory but no page asks for it.
The notification's reference number is shaped GBN-AG-YY-XXXXXX, where the six-character body uses Crockford base32 (0-9 and A-Z without I, L, O or U).
A notification must hold at least one commodity line, and an empty list is refused under the code obligation.commodityLine.atLeastOne.
claims.note: The commodity lines group states no upper limit on the number of lines.

claims.statement: Every commodity line must carry a commodity code.
Every commodity line must carry a species Latin name.
A commodity line's species common name is optional.
Every commodity line must carry a number of animals.
A line's number of packages is asked only when that line's commodity code is in the package-count list, and even then it is optional.
The county parish holding number is asked, and mandatory, when any commodity line's code is in the CPH-required list, and is out of scope otherwise.
Whether the consignment contains unweaned animals is asked once for the whole notification, and only when any commodity line's code is in the unweaned list.

Each animal identifier record inside a commodity line must carry at least one of seven identifiers: a microchip, a passport, a tattoo, an ear tag, a horse name, identification details or a description; an empty record is refused under obligation.unitRecord.identifiersRequired.

The at-least-one-identifier floor is stood down unless more than one commodity line has a code in the identified list, so a consignment with a single identified line is not held to it at the collection level.
claims.quote:
floorAppliesToParent: moreThanOne(
      allowListed(commodityCode, identifiedCommodityCodes, null)
    )
---
 * The inner gate names the entries that would be asked; this wrapper stands
 * the whole rule down unless there are at least two of them, and otherwise
 * hands back the inner decision untouched with the same `fulfilmentIndexes`.
claims.note: mechanism: works on the commodity-lines collection. moreThanOne returns the inner allowListed decision only when it admits more than one entry, and otherwise reports out of scope.

claims.statement: A microchip is asked of an animal only on lines whose commodity code is in the microchip list, and is optional there.
A passport is asked of an animal only on lines whose commodity code is in the passport list, and is optional there.
A tattoo is asked of an animal only on lines whose commodity code is in the tattoo list, and is optional there.
An ear tag is asked of an animal only on lines whose commodity code is in the ear-tag list, and is optional there.
A horse name is asked of an animal only when its line's commodity code and species Latin name together are in the horse-name list, and is optional there.
claims.quote:
export const horseName = {
  id: HORSE_NAME_ID,
  name: 'horseName',
  within: unitRecord,
  status: 'optional',
  applyTo: allowListedPairs(
    commodityCode,
    speciesLatinName,
    horseNameCodeSpecies,
    unitRecord,
    [horseNameReason]
  )
}

claims.statement: Identification details are asked of an animal only on lines whose commodity code is outside the identified list, and are optional there.
A free-text description is asked of an animal only on lines whose commodity code is outside the identified list, and is optional there.
A permanent address is asked of an animal, and is mandatory, when its line's commodity code and species pair is in the permanent-address list.

const permanentAddressPairGate = (reasons) =>
  allowListedPairs(
    commodityCode,
    speciesLatinName,
    permanentAddressCodeSpecies,

  id: '3fcbd0e6-f708-4c2c-89ab-a56c7e8ea0b7',
  name: 'permanentAddress',
  within: unitRecord,
  status: 'mandatory',

claims.statement: A trader can attach between zero and fifteen accompanying documents to a notification, and a sixteenth is refused under obligation.accompanyingDocument.tooMany.
The fifteen-document cap is enforced on the stored notification as well as on the page's Add affordance, so a saved notification holding more than the cap is still caught afterwards.
Each accompanying document must carry its own type, attachment type, reference and date of issue; all four are mandatory within a document.
A document's upload id and filename are optional, so a document can be recorded without a file attached.
The V4 data dictionary page still reads as if a notification can hold at most one accompanying document, and the obligation model is treated as the authority until that page is amended.
claims.note: An existing ruling recorded in code: a known disagreement with the V4 source, resolved in favour of the model.

claims.statement: Each document's instance id is a session-scoped counter value such as doc1 or doc2.
claims.quote: // Instance ids are session-scoped counter values (`doc1`, `doc2`, …).

claims.statement: A trader searching for a commodity gets one page of species grouped by CN code, with the total, the page number and the page size alongside.
claims.quote:
/**
 * One page of the species matching a term, grouped by CN code.
 *
 * @param {string} term - the search term.
 * @param {{page?: number, size: number}} paging - the zero-based page and its size.
 * @returns {Promise<{total: number, page: number, size: number, groups: Array<{code: string, species: Array<{latinName: string, commonName: string|null}>}>}>} the page of results.
 * @throws {import('@hapi/boom').Boom} 503 when reference data fails.
 */

claims.statement: The commodity search asks the reference data service for GET /commodities with the search term as q and the page and size as query parameters.
The species check asks the reference data service for POST /commodities/species-check with the commodity lines in the body.
The species check returns the commodity lines whose Latin name is not listed under their commodity code, and an empty list when every line's species is listed.
claims.quote:
/**
 * @param {Array<{code: string, latinName: string}>} lines - the lines to check.
 * @returns {Promise<Array<{code: string, latinName: string}>>} the lines whose
 *   Latin name is not listed under their code; empty when all are listed.
 * @throws {import('@hapi/boom').Boom} 503 when reference data fails.
 */

claims.statement: No species check is made at all when there are no commodity lines to check.
A species-check reply that carries no unlisted list is treated as a failure rather than as 'nothing unlisted'.

When the service is run in stub mode both the commodity search and the species check are answered from the service's own fixtures instead of reference data, and stub mode is never honoured in production.
A reference data failure is turned into a 503 'Reference data unavailable' naming the dataset that failed, either 'commodities' or 'species'.

Six commodity codes carry per-animal identifiers: cattle 0102 (ear tag, passport, tattoo), horses 0101 (microchip, passport and a horse name for Equus cabalus), swine 0103 (ear tag, tattoo), sheep 010410 (ear tag), goats 010420 (ear tag) and other live mammals 01061900 (microchip, passport, tattoo).
Those same six codes are the identified list, so a commodity line with any other code is treated as unidentified and asked for identification details and a description instead.
claims.quote: export const IDENTIFIED_CODES = Object.keys(COMMODITY_IDENTIFIERS)

claims.statement: The horse name is asked only for the species named Equus cabalus under commodity code 0101.

...
const HORSE_NAME_SPECIES = 'Equus cabalus'
...

Horses (0101) ask for a package count but do not require a CPH number; the three 0407 egg codes require a CPH number but ask for no package count.

claims.note: Cats, dogs and ferrets, in Latin.

claims.statement: Four commodity codes carry a description: 0101 'Live horses, asses, mules and hinnies', 0102 'Live bovine animals', 01061900 'Other live animals' and 0301 'Live fish'.
Three commodity codes carry a short name: 0101 'Horse', 0102 'Cattle' and 0301 'Fish'.
Live fish, commodity code 0301, has a description and a short name but no identifiers, so a fish consignment is asked for identification details and a description rather than a tag or passport.

claims.statement: The per-identifier code lists are derived from the one identifier table rather than written out, so a code that carries an identifier is always in that identifier's list.
claims.note: mechanism: turns the identifier table into per-identifier code lists, and into code-and-species pairs for an identifier that names a species.

claims.statement: A commodity search in stub mode matches a group when the term is a prefix of its CN code, and otherwise matches a species when every word of the term is a prefix of consecutive words of its Latin or common name.
claims.note: mechanism: the stub's own matching over the captured commodity fixtures; an empty term matches nothing by name, and a code prefix match returns the group's whole species list.

claims.statement: Stub search results are paged by slicing the flattened matches and then regrouping them by code, so a group can be split across two pages and the total counts species rather than groups.
claims.note: mechanism: paging over the stub's flattened code-and-species matches.

claims.statement: In stub mode a commodity line counts as unlisted when the captured fixtures hold no group with that code carrying that exact Latin name.
claims.quote:
const listedInStub = ({ code, latinName }) =>
  COMMODITY_GROUPS.some(
    (group) =>
      group.code === code &&
      group.species.some((species) => species.latinName === latinName)
  )

export const unlistedLinesInStub = (lines) =>
  lines.filter((line) => !listedInStub(line))

claims.statement: The stub's commodity groups are captured fixtures of the real reference data rather than a hand-written list.
claims.quote:
import { commodityGroups } from '../../../../services/_capture/fixtures.js'

export const COMMODITY_GROUPS = commodityGroups

claims.statement: The commodity service's own test support shows a ferret search returning two species under code 01061900, 'Mustela spp.' described as 'Weasels (including ermines, polecats, ferrets, and related species)' and 'Mustela putorius furo' described as 'Ferret'.
The commodity reference calls are tested at the network boundary, by mocking fetch rather than the service's own modules.
The system feature contributes one binding, the notification's approved reference number, held as a single value rather than a collection.
A commodity line is stored as a commodity code, a species Latin name, a species common name, a number of packages, a number of animals and a list of animal identifier records.
An accompanying document is stored as its type, its attachment type, its reference, a day-month-year date of issue and a filename.

A consignment party is stored as a name with a nested address, and some parties also carry a phone number and an email address; an address can be held either as free address lines with a country name or as lines with a town, postcode and country code.
claims.note: Two address shapes appear side by side in one finished notification, one keyed on `country` with free lines and one keyed on `countryCode` with a town and postcode.

claims.statement: A commercial transporter is stored as a name, an approval number and an address; a private transporter as a name and an address that also carries a phone number and an email address.
claims.quote:
"transporterType": "Commercial",

claims.statement: Every request to the set is checked by the journey entry guard before the page runs, and a request that fails it is redirected away rather than served.
The set refuses to start if any of its configuration seams is unfilled or any of its journey cookies is unregistered, so a misconfigured journey fails at boot rather than serving half a journey.

* Refuse to mount a set that has not configured every required seam or
 * registered every journey cookie.
claims.note: mechanism: checks the set's own registration against the seam registry and the Hapi server's cookie states at mount time; it works on configuration, not on a notification's data.

claims.statement: Every notification must say what is being imported — its commodity type — and the question applies whatever the answer.
claims.note: Collected by the commodity-type page; every other commodity-type gate in the manifest reads this one answer.

claims.statement: A notification must carry at least one commodity line, and a notification with no line at all is refused with the code obligation.commodityLines.atLeastOne.
claims.note: This is the manifest's one cardinality rule, and its one group: it is always in scope and is collected by the commodities list.

claims.statement: The commodity lines are a group that is always in scope, and a notification holding no line satisfies it vacuously as far as the fields below it are concerned.
Every commodity line must say which category it is, and that answer decides which of the other per-line questions the line is asked.
claims.note: Collected by the commodities feature, whose bindings own the ten per-line leaves.

claims.statement: Every commodity line must carry a quantity, whichever category it is, and it is the one per-line field with no category condition.

Genus, species, commodity code, potato variety, potato intended use, EPPO code, size of tree and phytosanitary treatments are each required on a commodity line only when the line's category asks for that field, and the list of categories that ask for it comes from the set's own commodity service rather than the manifest.
claims.quote:
const gatedOnCategory = (id, name) => ({
  id,
  name,
  within: commodityLine,
  status: 'mandatory',
  applyTo: allowListed(
    category,
    () => categoriesRequiring(name),
    null,
    appliesBecauseCategory(name)
  )
})
claims.note: Ids: genus d6903f3a-8e5b-4127-8d74-3f1e9b5a0c48, species e7a14b4b-9f6c-4238-9e85-401fac6b1d59, commodityCode f8b25c5c-a07d-4349-8f96-512abd7c2e6a, potatoVariety 09c36d6d-b18e-445a-9007-623bce8d3f7b, potatoIntendedUse 1ad47e7e-c29f-456b-8118-734cdf9e408c, eppoCode 2be58f8f-d3a0-467c-9229-845de0af519d, sizeOfTree 3cf69090-e4b1-478d-833a-956ef1b062ae, phytosanitaryTreatments 4d07a1a1-f5c2-489e-944b-a67f02c173bf. Each is mandatory within commodityLine. All eight, with category and quantity, are collected by the commodities feature.

claims.statement: Each per-line field's reason for applying is recorded in the words "<field> applies on lines whose category asks for it", under the code obligation.<field>.applicable.becauseCategory.
Which categories ask for a per-line field is looked up only when the rule is checked, so the manifest reads no reference data when the service starts.
claims.quote:
* A per-line field scoped to the categories the set-owned service says ask for
 * it. The allow-list is read lazily, at gate execution: an obligation module
 * does no IO and reads no reference data when it loads.

claims.statement: A notification carries one country of origin for the whole consignment, whatever its commodity type, and must give it.
claims.note: Id 5e18b2b2-06d3-49af-a55c-b78013d284c0, status mandatory, no applyTo. Collected by the origin page.

claims.statement: Which countries a particular category may come from — ware potatoes from four countries, conifer wood without bark from four others, everything else from an EU member State — is checked on the origin page against the set's own commodity service, not by the manifest's rules, because the category sits on each commodity line while the origin is one answer for the notification.
Whether the consignment has already arrived in Great Britain is asked only of notifications for plants for planting and for wood and cut trees.
claims.quote:
explanation:
      'arrivalStatus applies to notifications for plants for planting and for wood and cut trees'
claims.note: Id 6f29c3c3-17e4-45b0-b66d-c89124e395d1, status mandatory, includesGate on commodityType with the reason code obligation.arrivalStatus.applicable.becauseCommodityType. Collected by the arrival-status page.

claims.statement: The notifier says whether the consignment has arrived rather than the service working it out from the arrival date, because one branch of the rules turns on arrival in the country and the other on arrival at the destination, and a date alone cannot tell them apart.
claims.quote:
* The notifier says so rather than the service deriving it from the arrival
 * date: reg 26(2)(a) branches on arrival in the country and reg 26(2)(b) on
 * arrival at the intended destination, and a date alone cannot say which
 * branch a consignment arriving today is in.

claims.statement: When a change of commodity type takes the arrival status out of scope, the answer already given is removed rather than kept.
claims.quote:
* A top-level scalar gate on a top-level scalar answer, so the whole
 * notification is either asked the question or not — the engine purges the
 * answer when a change of commodity type takes it out of scope.

claims.statement: Every notification must give an arrival date, whatever its commodity type, and the three different ways the question is worded are a matter for the arrival-details page, not for the rule.
claims.quote:
* One obligation for every commodity type, because every notification owes a
 * date: reg 24A(2)(a) asks potatoes for the expected date, and reg 26(2)(a)
 * asks plants and wood for the expected date of landing or, once the
 * consignment is here, the date it first arrived. Which of those three
 * sentences a notifier is shown is the arrival-details page's business — the
 * matter owed is the same one.
claims.note: Id 63e22d64-b9a0-40b4-aec6-0f5f48bdd556, status mandatory, no applyTo. Collected by the arrival-details page.

claims.statement: An expected time of arrival is asked only of potato notifications, and the answer is removed if the notification changes to another commodity type.
claims.quote:
* Reg 24A(2)(a) asks potatoes for 'the expected time and date of their
 * arrival'. Reg 26(2)(a) asks plants and wood for a date alone, so the time is
 * a potato matter and the engine purges it when a notification changes to
 * another commodity type.
claims.note: Id 0d05c100-b887-4a12-8251-673bc1e1ac31, status mandatory, equalsGate on commodityType = potatoes, reason code obligation.arrivalTime.applicable.becauseCommodityType with the words 'arrivalTime applies to notifications for potatoes'. Collected by the arrival-details page.

claims.statement: A proposed place of landing is asked only of potato notifications; plants and wood are never asked for one.
claims.quote:
* Reg 24A(2)(aa) is the only landing element in the statute; reg 26(2) has
 * none, so plants and wood are never asked. Gated the same way as the time, on
 * the same notification-level answer.
claims.note: Id 1c706e7c-6d61-4e47-8bb4-e53efcd72809, status mandatory, equalsGate on commodityType = potatoes, reason code obligation.proposedPlaceOfLanding.applicable.becauseCommodityType with the words 'proposedPlaceOfLanding applies to notifications for potatoes'. Collected by the arrival-details page.

claims.statement: Every notification must give one place of destination — where the consignment is going, or where it is being kept once it is here — and which of those three questions the notifier is shown is decided from the arrival status by the page, not by the rule.
claims.note: Id 7eb0d717-f852-43f7-9377-c6a9c301d702, status mandatory, no applyTo. Collected by the place-of-destination picker.
